name: Lakeland Corridor
inspired_by: The Suwalki Gap as of 2026: the roughly 65 km land corridor along the Polish-Lithuanian border between Russia's Kaliningrad exclave and Belarus. Glacial lakeland of hills, lakes and forests, farmland and small towns, crossed by one main highway and one railway, with fortified borders on both flanks (fences, cameras, new defence lines). The map compresses the corridor so both flank borders sit on its edges. All towns are fictional.
climate: Humid continental (Koppen Dfb), one of the coldest parts of lowland Poland: summers 17-23 C, winters -5 to -12 C with snow cover from December to March; 550-650 mm precipitation; frequent morning fog over lakes.
seasons: Winter (Dec-Mar): snow, frozen lakes thick enough to walk on in cold spells, short days
Spring (Apr-May): thaw, mud on field tracks, high water in streams
Summer (Jun-Aug): warm, green, lake tourists and kayakers, haymaking
Autumn (Sep-Nov): harvest, rain, fog, early dusk

vegetation: rye, oats, potato and maize fields

terrain.relief: Rolling glacial terrain: moraine hills to 300 m, kettle-hole lakes and long ribbon lakes in tunnel valleys, eskers, boulder fields; steep short slopes with long open fields between forest blocks.
features: border fence with patrol road and cameras on both flank edges
new anti-tank ditches, dragon's teeth and bunkers near the borders
the tripoint area where three borders meet at the south-west corner
terrain.water: Many lakes (5-15% of area), a few small rivers and streams, drainage ditches; lakes freeze in cold winters.

generator.approach: Heightmap at 10 m. Rolling fbm base; ribbon lakes carved as elongated troughs along NNE-SSW and filled to a water level; kettle lakes as cellular depressions; eskers as warped ridges; boulders instanced. Border lines placed as splines on the west and east edges.
generator.rivers: Small streams by flow accumulation linking lakes; water level per lake basin computed by fill.
generator.settlement_flattening: Villages on gentle hill flanks and lake shores, flattened lightly per plot.
generator.notes: The single highway and railway through the corridor are the strategic chokepoints; lakes and forests channel movement into 2-3 east-west lanes. Open fields between forest edges are long kill zones for drones and ATGMs.

settlements.architecture: Market town: a central square with a baroque church, two- and three-storey brick and plastered tenements with tiled roofs, communist-era four- and five-storey blocks, single-family houses with gabled roofs, a supermarket and petrol station on the highway, a railway station.
settlements.wall_class: Brick tenements medium-thick; concrete blocks thick; timber annexes thin.
layout_rules: market square with church and town hall
blocks and houses on the outskirts
lake shore with beach and boat hire

settlements.architecture: Farm villages: one-and-a-half-storey houses of brick or timber with steep roofs, barns of fieldstone and timber, Lithuanian wooden roadside shrines and Polish wayside crosses, a small church or chapel; farm machinery sheds.
settlements.wall_class: Fieldstone barns thick; brick houses medium; timber thin.
layout_rules: street village along a road with long field strips behind each farm
chapel and bus stop at the centre

settlements.architecture: Isolated modern farmsteads: a house, large steel-clad cattle barns, silage clamps, grain silos.
layout_rules: on hilltops with long views, one track in

settlements.architecture: Military and border sites: a brigade base in the forest (sheds, barracks, a fuel park), border guard stations with fence control rooms, bunkers and dragon's teeth, a highway border crossing (now quiet) with customs canopies, an air-defence site.
settlements.wall_class: Bunkers thick; sheds thin; teeth block vehicles.
layout_rules: border stations on the flank edges every 5-8 km
brigade base in the forest near the highway
defence-line belts 1-3 km in from each border

infrastructure.roads: One expressway-standard highway (Via Baltica-type) north-south through the corridor, regional roads, gravel field and forest tracks; small bridges over streams between lakes are chokepoints.
infrastructure.rail: One line through the corridor with a new European-gauge section under construction and a break-of-gauge yard.
infrastructure.power: Overhead lines and a new interconnector substation; wind farms on hills.
infrastructure.airfields: None on the map; a highway strip proposal for allied aircraft (AI only).
infrastructure.checkpoints: Border guard stations, fence cameras and patrol roads on both flanks; the main road crossing is the only official crossing on the map; military traffic control on the highway in escalation.

pois.description: Five-metre steel fence with razor wire, cameras on masts, a patrol road and a border guard pickup; forest on both sides.
Highway bridge between two lakes; the only fast route north for allied reinforcements.
Break-of-gauge rail yard with sidings, cranes, transshipment sheds and fuel tanks.
Allied brigade base in pine forest: vehicle sheds with tanks and IFVs, barracks, fuel park, training lanes.
pois.contract_use: contract board; recover lost equipment or sensitive kit (clients deu, nld, usa)

pois.description: Wooded hill where three borders meet, with a monument, a viewpoint tower and fences converging.
Field where smuggling balloons from across the border come down; scattered packages, tracks to a barn used by a smuggling ring.
pois.contract_use: counter-smuggling raid and evidence recovery (client ltu)

pois.description: New bunkers, dragon's teeth rows and an anti-tank ditch along a forest edge facing the border.
Lake resort with wooden cabins, a jetty, a restaurant and a camping field; summer crowds.
Isolated farm used by a sabotage team: barn workshop, a van with false plates, radios and drones.
pois.contract_use: counter-sabotage raid with police (clients pol, ltu)

pois.description: Hilltop air-defence site with radar and launcher vehicles, fence and a generator.
pois.contract_use: site security during a drone incursion

pois.description: Interconnector substation with transformers, a control building and a fenced yard.

weather.visibility_notes: Fog over lakes and valleys at dawn; snow shows tracks; winter nights long.

civilians.behaviour: Sparse rural population; farmers in fields, lorries on the highway, summer tourists at lakes; border closures keep the area quiet. Irregular border-crossing groups occasionally appear near the fence (civilians, never targets). Residents report strangers to the border guard.
civilians.casualty_risk_notes: Low density, but lakeside resorts in summer and towns raise risk; civilians near the fence are a strict no-fire case.

factions_present.where: Southern half of the corridor: border guard stations, defence-line bunkers, air defence.
Northern half: border stations, rail yard, highway bridge.
Brigade forest base in the northern half (permanent German brigade).
Rotational armoured units at the base and air defence in the southern half.
Liaison and logistics movement through the corridor toward the Canadian-led brigade further north.
Beyond the west-edge border (Kaliningrad side): border posts, drones, electronic warfare, sabotage teams.
Beyond the east-edge border: border posts, exercises, balloon and drone incursions, pressure on the fence.

frontline: Two hostile flanks and a friendly corridor. In the grey-zone state, rus and blr events (drones, balloons, GPS jamming, fence pressure, sabotage teams) raise alert in edge zones and post border, counter-smuggling and counter-sabotage contracts. In the late-game escalation scenario (proposed), rus and blr push from both edges to close the corridor at the highway bridge and rail yard; allied units hold the lakes and defence lines, and the war sim measures corridor control as the share of the highway still open.
contract_hooks: Border security patrol along the fence during a pressure event (clients ltu, pol)
Counter-smuggling raid on a balloon landing site and barn (client ltu)
Counter-sabotage raid on a farmstead safe house (clients pol, ltu)
Guard the rail yard or substation against sabotage (clients ltu, pol)
Recover sensitive kit lost in a forest training area (clients deu, nld, usa)
Air-defence site security during a drone incursion (client pol)
Escalation scenario: hold the highway bridge until reinforcements cross (late game)

hot_zones.name: Corridor escalation (late game, fictional what-if)
hot_zones.layout: Two enemy HQs off the edges; 4-6 bridgehead outposts at lake gaps; checkpoints on regional roads; roaming recon and drone teams; 2 QRF armour groups; allied brigade base as the friendly anchor

insertion.fob: FOB at the allied brigade forest base. Good road network; helicopters affected by fog and EW threat; AAVs can cross lakes (proposed) but not frozen-and-cracking ice.

early_game_notes: Peer-state flanks (rus late, blr late); late-campaign theatre.
ambient_audio: ice cracking on lakes in winter
